title: Rays acquire Peralta from Mets as deadline play for AL East contention
dek: The Tampa Bay Rays acquired right-hander Freddy Peralta from the New York Mets in a trade sending three prospects to New York. Peralta, a two-time All-Star, has underperformed with the Mets this season but brings past postseason pedigree to the Rays' rotation push.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Tampa Bay Rays acquired right-hander Freddy Peralta from the New York Mets, sending outfielder Aidan Smith, infielder Emilien Pitre, and right-hander Gary Gill Hill in return.
bottom_line: The Rays added a former All-Star with an all-star resume but current struggling numbers. Watch whether Peralta stabilizes his performance in Tampa Bay's system and whether the rotation depth proves sufficient for a late-season AL East push.
body: The Tampa Bay Rays acquired right-hander Freddy Peralta from the New York Mets on August 2, 2026, according to ESPN's reporting. The Mets received three prospects in return: outfielder Aidan Smith, infielder Emilien Pitre, and right-hander Gary Gill Hill.

Peralta, 30, is a two-time All-Star who brings established postseason experience but arrives at the deadline after a disappointing 2026 season with New York. In 22 starts for the Mets, Peralta is 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA and 113 strikeouts, per ESPN. The durability concerns are material: he has pitched into the sixth inning in only 11 of his 22 starts and completed five innings in just 15.

The contrast with his career peak is stark. In his previous career-best season with the Milwaukee Brewers, Peralta posted a 2.70 ERA in 176 and two-thirds innings. The Rays are betting on a regression to that form rather than the continuation of his 2026 struggles.

Peralta is a free agent this offseason, meaning the Rays are acquiring a short-term rental ahead of what could be a tight AL East race. He will join Drew Rasmussen, Shane McClanahan, and Nick Martinez in the Rays' rotation. The trade also marks Tampa Bay's quick pivot after missing out on acquiring Tarik Skubal, according to CBS Sports' reporting.
Peralta was previously acquired by the Mets along with Tobias Myers in a deal that sent two top prospects to the Brewers, making this his second trade in a single offseason.
